metadata.title: Micron's AI Demand Problem Is a Good One

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Memory-chip maker Micron Technology Inc. (MU, Financials) says demand from AI customers is running way ahead of what it can deliver at now. Data center clients are requesting about 50% more memory than Micron can promise it would provide, a sign that the market is very tight, CEO Sanjay Mehrotra told CNBC.That's a big change for an industry that has long experienced cycles of boom and bust. "AI technologies require more memory, faster memory, and lower power consumption, making memory more and more critical to the buildout of AI infrastructure, said Mehrotra. Memory is a strategic infrastructure of the AI era, he called it.Demand is also moving beyond traditional data centers. Other development areas, said Mehrotra, include autonomous vehicles, robots, and AI-enabled consumer gadgets. The comments come after Micron said it was spending more on research and manufacturing in the U.S.The business recently announced Micron Research Labs in Boise, backed by an anticipated $10 billion investment over the next 10 years. The center will focus on advanced memory technologies, packaging, computing architectures, and future semiconductor manufacturing.Micron had previously also announced more than $250 billion of anticipated U.S. manufacturing and research investment. But the most crucial number for investors is the 50% demand gap. If consumers continue to want significantly more memory than Micron can provide, restricted supply might maintain pricing and assist extend the present memory upcycle further than past cycles.
